OTA-1882 — the paste fits in the window

The owner's title screen offered `CRASHED SAVE CAPTURED · screen-render · 60m ago ·
420072 bytes` with a COPY CRASHED SAVE button. He pressed it and could not paste the
result anywhere. A diagnostic nobody can deliver is not a diagnostic.

THE 420,072 WAS NOT THE CLIPBOARD, AND THE CLIPBOARD WAS WORSE. That number is
`capture.raw.length` — UTF-16 code units of the RETAINED save, printed beside the
word "bytes" while counting something else. The clipboard is a different object
entirely: on the normal parse-OK path it is `JSON.stringify({ player, worldMemory })`
with the gameLog excluded. Measured on a real 607,188-byte save, the old export was
405,288 bytes; the new one is 10,091. And measured against the owner's own ingested
COPY evidence (player-log_2026-08-25T02-07-26, 59,818 UTF-8 bytes), 95.9% of an
export is that one blob, with the growth all legitimate play:

  player.inventory          21,372 B   37.3%   71 items
  worldMemory.visitedRooms  10,598 B   18.5%   18 rooms
  worldMemory.worldEvents    8,629 B   15.0%   50 events
  worldMemory.recentRaids    2,614 B    4.6%   12 raids
  worldMemory.patrols        2,076 B    3.6%   25 patrols

SO THE DEFECT WAS A MISSING CEILING, NOT A LEAK. Every sibling diagnostic path here
owns a budget — LOG_CHARS_CAP 40,000 for the email paste, FULL_LOG_CHARS_CAP 200,000
for the Sentry push, INVENTORY_CHARS_CAP 12,000, LOG_ATTACHMENT_MAX_CHARS 800,000,
CRASH_LEDGER_CAP 10. The owner-facing clipboard was the only export with none. It has
one now: 40,000 UTF-8 BYTES, taken from this project's own human-paste precedent
rather than invented, and measured in bytes because that is what the destination
counts. `.length` is not a byte count; one emoji is four bytes and a length of two.

⚠⚠⚠ AND THE EVIDENCE IS UNTOUCHED, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT. `raw` in
`@tartaria/lastCrashSave` is the only copy of a save that can never be loaded
(OTA-341/343), so nothing here trims it — not at capture, not at retention. The full
bundle already reaches us independently; the owner's own log recorded it going out by
itself, `#mufzsk25hsud cleared from disk`. So the compact paste does not have to CARRY
the state. It has to NAME it.

⚠⚠ WHICH IS WHY THERE IS A CORRELATION KEY, AND WHY IT IS NOT `bundleId`. The relay's
bundle id is `${Date.now().toString(36)}${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,6)}` —
it contains randomness, it is minted at send-staging time, and in this very incident
it did not exist when the capture was written, because the process died first and the
push happened on the next boot 21 seconds later. Reading "the newest pending bundle"
at COPY time would bind a crashed save to whatever an adjacent crash, a manual SEND
LOG or a retry last touched. So the key is the crash's own facts — `ts` and `kind` —
through one leaf helper that BOTH the ledger and the capture call, and the same two
values already travel to us inside the relayed crash-ledger summary. Zero change to
sentryTransport; no new tag, no new service, no reverse lookup.

IT IS A CORRELATION KEY, NOT A UNIQUE ID, AND IT SAYS SO. Two crashes of the same
kind in the same millisecond resolve to one key — which is exactly what `recordCrash`
has always deduped them to, on purpose, so a re-entered `hydrate()` cannot invent a
crash that never happened. The suite pins that real contract instead of a stronger
claim a future reader would trust wrongly.

THE OVERSIZED PATHS ARE BUILT STRUCTURALLY, NEVER BY CUTTING JSON. A chopped
`JSON.stringify` is unparseable, says nothing about what it dropped, and is
indistinguishable from corruption — the one thing a crash report must never fake.
Chronological collections keep their newest entries; current-state collections say so
rather than passing a head slice off as the whole pack; every partial rendering states
its original, retained and omitted counts. The corrupt-save path keeps a bounded
head-anchored excerpt with its true omitted byte count, repairs nothing, reformats
nothing, and says the full malformed bytes are still on the device.

REPORTS ALREADY UNDER BUDGET ARE NOT TOUCHED — same envelope, same HIGHLIGHTS, same
FULL STATE JSON, plus the correlation line. The bounded assembler becomes visible only
when size demands it.

AND THE CARD'S LABEL IS NOW TRUE. It measures UTF-8 bytes. That number is the retained
artifact and stays a separate concept from the paste budget; the card never mentions
the budget.

  app/diagnostics/crashCorrelation.ts   the leaf both paths call
  app/diagnostics/portableReport.ts     the byte budget, the assembler, the
                                        collection semantics
  app/diagnostics/crashSave.ts          correlationId on the capture; bounded
                                        parse-OK and parse-fail exports
  app/diagnostics/crashLedger.ts        calls the helper for its id (output
                                        byte-identical)
  App.tsx                               ONE timestamp per crash, threaded to both
                                        writers on the boundary and fatal paths
  app/screens/TitleScreen.tsx           the card counts the unit it prints

  ota1882ThePasteFitsInTheWindow   40/40 — correlation determinism and the honest
                                   collision contract, small-report compatibility,
                                   oversized parse-OK, oversized parse-fail, Unicode,
                                   budget boundaries incl. the notices' own cost,
                                   recovery untouched, relay untouched, the card's unit
  directly affected contracts      8 suites, 168/168 (crashSaveCapture, saveSnapshot,
                                   crashLedger, sentryTransport, bugReport ×2, 1847)
  fast surface                     1381/1381 suites · 16,162 passed · 3 skipped
  typecheck:ci                     exit 0
  typecheck:tests                  OK — at baseline (196), no growth
  lint                             clean
  check gates                      22/22

FIVE NEGATIVE CONTROLS, none committed, all six production files restored
byte-identically (md5 verified 6/6). NC1 restore the unbounded full-state COPY — 5 red.
NC2 drop the correlation key — 4 red. NC3 let capture and ledger read the clock
separately — 1 red, the exact defect the threading exists to prevent. NC4 truncate by
characters instead of bytes — 2 red on multibyte content. NC5 stop protecting
Priority 1 — 6 red.

FOUR ASSEMBLER DEFECTS THE SUITE CAUGHT IN MY OWN FIRST DRAFT, worth recording because
each is a way a cap leaks. The omission notice was appended AFTER the accounting
(measured 345 against a 300 budget). The over-budget marker's length was estimated
instead of measured, landing one byte over. Both are now paid for out of the same
allowance they describe, and a final unconditional clamp guarantees the ceiling even if
some future path miscounts.

TWO NEIGHBOUR CONTRACTS TURNED RED AND NEITHER WAS WEAKENED. ota1380CrashLedger pinned
the byte-exact text `captureActiveCrashSave(`fatal:${stage}`)` and the fatal handler now
also passes a correlation id; its own sibling assertion two lines below was already
written in the open form, so the fatal pin was aligned to match and still pins the stage
argument. ota1484APinStatesAClaim counts fixtures that set `currentLocationId` without
coordinates, shrink-only at 54, and this package's fixture made it 55 — so the fixture
spread `placedAt`, which is what that pin's own instruction asks for. The baseline was
not moved.

⚠ AND ONE INSTRUMENT DEFECT OF MINE, TWICE, both the OTA-1721 class: a census that
scanned unstripped source convicted this package's own comments for naming the things
they exist to forbid. Comments are stripped first now — and one assertion had to stop
forbidding the word "repair" altogether, because the corrupt-save report's honest
sentence is "NOT repaired, NOT reformatted" and that is code, not a comment. It pins
the absent mechanisms instead.

ADJACENT, REPORTED NOT FIXED: COPY SAVE on the About screen shares the same unbounded
`buildSaveSnapshot` blob and keeps it. #214 was scoped to the crashed-save path, and
widening it silently would have been a different package wearing this one's number.

NOT CLAIMED: physical clipboard/paste verification on the owner's hardware.
